Study-002 · R4 intervention design and simulation · virtual Patient 2

Virtual surgery and stimulation on Patient 2: simulation results (A0038)

Every prespecified virtual treatment (ablation, disconnection, SEEG sustained-current and 50 Hz pulse-train stimulation) was simulated on the A0018 MAP ensemble with a TVB re-implementation of the Wang et al. 2025 stimulation model. Each treatment is compared with the no-treatment run of the same model optimum.

Batch A0038-SimulationBatch · committed by R4 in task T0017, finished 15:52 UTCGate status: · unreviewedLedger snapshot 2026-11-01 16:19 UTC (study still running)Release rel-f02dbe461251
EXPLORATORY: MODEL NOT QUALIFIED. These are research simulations on a virtual patient, not clinical recommendations. No prediction may be frozen on this batch.
  • The inversion model failed its benchmark. A0037 (R3's synthetic qualification benchmark of the v2 AR(1) model): NOT QUALIFIED. planted EZ (44) ranks 2nd by pooled posterior mean x0 (PZ region 40 1st); P(rank 1) for EZ 0.026; max x0 R-hat 4.73, all 162 x0 R-hat >= 1.05, min bulk ESS 17. R5's gate on A0037 is still pending.
  • The simulated patient does not look like the recording. In the median optimum, the 10 most active simulated SEEG channels share 0/10 (post window) and 0/10 (full window) channels with the recording. The simulated recorded protocol (STIM-PT amp 1) also overlaps 0/10.
  • The inputs are not a posterior. A0018 is a preliminary MAP ensemble of optimizer end points, not posterior draws, and it is not qualified. The NUTS fit A0019 did not converge in either window.

Findings

For clinicians

  • The primary (post-stimulation) window is uninformative. None of the 24 model optima seized without treatment, so no treatment could reduce anything. All 16 finite arms tie for first.
  • In the full-window sensitivity analysis (12 optima, median 3.5 seizing regions without treatment), removing the estimated EZ plus the two propagation regions (9 regions) helped most: median -3.0 seizing regions (5–95%: -4.9 to -1.6). It abolished all seizures in 42% of optima.
  • Disconnecting the same regions was weaker than ablating them (median -1.0).
  • Sustained-current SEEG stimulation at contact R7-8 gave -1.0 to -0.5 regions and never abolished seizures.
  • 50 Hz pulse trains did not reduce seizing regions. Applied for the whole horizon they lengthened total seizure time (median +3.9 to +4.8 s). The higher amplitudes failed numerically.
  • Targets are model regions (Left-Orbito-frontal-cortex, Left-F2-rostral, Left-Anterior-cingulate-cortex, Left-STS-anterior, Right-Orbito-frontal-cortex, Right-Gyrus-rectus, Right-Anterior-cingulate-cortex), not surgical volumes. Amplitudes are model units, not mA.

For engineers

  • The simulator is p2sim 1.0: TVB 2.10 at region level, the package SpatEpiStim model, Heun integration at dt 0.05 ms, Heaviside coupling a = 0.1·K, and gain-weighted biphasic 50 Hz StimuliRegion. Its self-test reproduces the package equations bitwise (T0015).
  • Every candidate was paired with its own baseline: same x0, K, initial state, horizon and noise seed. Effects are candidate minus baseline per optimum. They were recomputed in finalize.py over finite runs only, with explicit ties. This page re-derives each median and 5–95% range from the per-run file and checks it against the payload.
  • Pulse-train arms with Istim ≥ 0.02–0.04 at the max-gain region went NaN at dt 0.05 ms. They are reported as failures, not dropped.
  • The x0 values come from a 2D-Epileptor fit and were inserted into the 6D+m generator model. This mismatch, together with the failed benchmark, is the main threat to validity.

1 · Design

The virtual patient

Patient 2 is Wang et al. 2025's simulated "virtual patient" (dataSim/Patient2, case record A0009). It has a 162-region VEP-atlas connectome, a 191-channel bipolar SEEG gain matrix, and a 12 s simulated recording at 125 Hz that contains a 50 Hz SEEG stimulation train from 0.5 to 3.5 s. There is no MRI and there are no electrode coordinates, so every target is a whole atlas region or a contact identified by its gain row. Its ground truth is sealed in the study vault and was not used here.

The model input is the A0018 MAP ensemble: 24 L-BFGS optima per fitted window. R3 named two windows before fitting: post (after the stimulation train, primary, horizon 7.76 s) and full (whole recording, sensitivity, horizon 14.4 s). Each horizon is twice the fitted window length.

Targets derived by R4 from A0018 with the prespecified rules (top-1 = highest median x0; EZ set = x0 > −2.06 in more than half of the optima). Source: payload.results.*.ez_estimate / derived.

Prespecification

  • Common spec work/amend/r4_common_spec.json, v2 (written 14:45 UTC), sha256 70ee917cacab98f42c37c092b9695b8d48ae52ed017a8bed0efd1b7751fa0461. This matches the hash recorded in every plan and in the batch metadata (✓ match).
  • Effect: Paired difference candidate - baseline per sample; report median and 90% interval across samples, and the fraction of samples where the candidate abolishes all seizures.
  • Ranking: Candidates ranked by median reduction in seizing regions, ties broken by total seizure duration; report rank stability across samples (fraction of samples in which each candidate ranks first).
  • Scenario set A0034 and request A0035 were committed at the start of T0017, before any result. The stopping rule was: one SimulationBatch covering all candidates on all optima of both windows by 16:45 UTC; if time runs out, the primary window is committed and the sensitivity window is reported as not run.

2 · Before and after: the median optimum

These panels show the full window's median optimum A0018-full-start7 (median by baseline seizure count). Rows are the 19 regions (of 162 simulated) that cross u1 = −1 in any arm, plus every targeted region. Colour is the fast variable u1 on one shared scale (colour bar): background-like is rest, blue is the −1 threshold, and the strongest contrast is above it. ● marks a region removed by that arm. Hover a heatmap for region, time and value.

A dark band means u1 went above −1. A region counts as seizing only when such excursions recur within 250 ms for at least 1 s, so the short rhythmic discharges seen in many rows are not counted as seizures.

4 · The two windows: post (primary) vs full (sensitivity)

Why the post window says nothing

No baseline seizures in any of 24 optima (x0 max ~ -2.28, sub-threshold in the 6D model). No candidate can reduce seizures; ranking uninformative (16 arms tied). STIM-PT amp <= 2 induced no seizure; amp 4 numerically failed.

A0018 already flagged the cause: Primary window violates the observation model's rest-at-first-observation assumption: 177/191 channels have their feature maximum at the first post-stimulation observation (power decays after the stim train). The frozen model then finds no supra-threshold node (H4-like) - this may be a model/data mismatch rather than evidence against an EZ.

The only non-zero post-window effect is in SEEG channel exceedance under the pulse trains. That is stimulation-driven activity, not seizure, and it appears in the table below and in the explorer.

5 · Failures, deviations and resolved ambiguities

Numerical failures

These arms went non-finite (NaN/Inf) during integration in at least one optimum. They are failures: the whole arm is excluded from effects and ranking, and it was neither dropped nor imputed. Every one is a 50 Hz pulse train at Istim ≥ 0.02 at the max-gain region. Payload numerical check: all_finite = false (post), false (full).

Deviations from the request (A0035)

  • Sensitivity window 'full' run on the 12 highest-lp of 24 optima (compute limit for 16:45 UTC; chosen before any full-window simulation ran). The other 12 were not simulated.
  • Pulse-train arms with Istim >= 0.02-0.04 at the max-gain region went non-finite at dt 0.05 ms (post: amp4 PT and chronic; full: amp2 and amp4 PT and chronic). They are recorded as numerical failures and excluded from effects and ranking, not dropped.
  • Effects and ranking recomputed in finalize.py from runs.json over finite paired runs, with explicit ties; p2sim's own summary.json (which includes non-finite arms and a tie-blind rank-first count) is superseded by this record.

The 12 simulated full-window optima are those with the highest log posterior, chosen before any full-window simulation ran (samples_full.json subset_rule). Their lp ranges from -3470.9 to -3431.6. The other 12 were never simulated, so the full-window spread probably understates the ensemble spread.

Spec ambiguities R4 resolved (T0015, before any model existed)

  • raw-gain weights numerically infeasible (Istim>0.04 -> NaN) so weights normalised and 1 unit = Istim 0.01
  • dt 0.1 inaccurate under pulses -> 0.05
  • biphasic = 1 ms/phase
  • seizure = u1 > -1 recurring within 250 ms for >= 1 s
  • SEEG log-power metric uses N(0,0.02) noise floor seeded 1000+i

Limitations recorded by R4

  • Preliminary MAP ensemble, model not qualified; predictions must not be frozen on this batch.
  • Generator/inverter mismatch: x0 from the 2D fit inserted into the 6D+m SpatEpiStim; coupling mapping a = 0.1*K is an R4 convention.
  • Stimulation amplitudes are model units (1 unit = Istim 0.01 at the max-gain region); raw gain weights were numerically infeasible.
  • Signals saved are 50 Hz block averages (the 50 Hz pulse artefact averages out).
  • Qualitative baseline check vs the recording failed in both windows (see results.*.qualitative_check_vs_recording).
  • Seizure metric counts direct stimulus-driven u1 excursions above -1 as seizure if sustained >= 1 s.
  • Signals file of each window contains the median sample's baseline and every arm, including non-finite (NaN) arms.

Need N001 (○ open, raised by R1): Vertex-to-region mapping from fsaverage5 (ico5, 10242 vertices/hemisphere) to the 162 VEP-atlas regions for the TI EMF maps in data/EMF. Acceptance: A documented, hashed mapping (or an explicit infeasibility decision by LEAD/R4) covering all 20484 vertices.

Possible second wave

Patient anatomy has since been downloaded to data/wang-co2-ana/ (9 files: elec/seeg.xyz, tvb/Cortex_pial_ico5.zip, tvb/Cortex_region_map_ico5.txt, tvb/Cortex_sphere_ico5.zip, tvb/connectivity.vep.zip, tvb/gain_dipole_ico5.npz, tvb/gain_region_map_ico5.txt, tvb/region_map_ico5.txt, tvb/stimulus_profile_vep_SEEG.pkl). It includes an ico5 region map with 20484 vertex rows, the same vertex count as the fsaverage5 EMF maps (2 × 10,242), plus an SEEG contact file and an ico5 dipole gain. If that surface is shown to be in fsaverage5 vertex correspondence and its labels match the 162 VEP regions, it could provide the documented mapping N001 asks for, and TI could be simulated in a second wave. None of this has been checked yet: R4 has not used these files, and N001 is still open.
